title: App Action step: its card on the canvas (#2339)
intro: The card an ops workflow's App Action step shows on the canvas: one catalogue action, such as Google Drive's List files, run through a saved connection. For whoever reads or builds an ops workflow. Settled by Dan on 2026-10-23 in two rounds, drawn on the real canvas in place of a Salesforce step's card.

requirements.text: An ops workflow's App Action step has a card of its own on the canvas that names the service and the action it runs.

chrome.from: http://localhost:3989/dev/app-action?frame=app-action-card at 1440 by 900 on main 063ab06, after data-preview-ready (zoom 1.0368, no step selected), the real WorkflowCanvas with the App Action step in place, its card removed and the slot left empty with the card's two connection handles kept, no sign in needed, 2026-10-23 (recaptured so the steps around the card sit where a real App Action card puts them; the rounds drew it in place of a Salesforce card on /dev/connection-field)

frames.title: The card of a step running Google Drive's List files, on the canvas

decisions.decision: The card's header names the service, Google Drive, and the action the step runs, List files, sits in a chip on the header's right.
decisions.why: Round 1: Dan chose "In the header" over showing nothing and over a line under the step's name, as the Salesforce card shows its operation.
decisions.check: The card's header reads the fixture's service, then a chip reading the fixture's action, the chip to the right of the service's name.

decisions.decision: The header carries the service's own mark, Google Drive's for Drive, on the plain beige header the uncommon steps use; the service's name is in ordinary case, not capitals, so it fits beside the chip, and the chip is gray 100 with gray 600 text.
decisions.why: Round 2: Dan chose "Service's own icon" over the plain box and over a tinted header, so the service is recognised at a glance while the card stays quiet.
decisions.check: The header's background is the beige of the canvas's uncommon steps, it holds Google Drive's mark (its blue part filled #0066da), the service's name is written as given with no capitals added, gray 600, and the chip is gray 100 with gray 600 text.

decisions.decision: Under the header the card reads the step's name, then its step id in monospace, as the other cards do.
decisions.check: Below its header the card reads exactly two lines, the fixture's label then its namespace, the namespace in a monospace font.

idioms: The card is drawn into the empty slot of an App Action step in a captured copy of the canvas at 1440 wide (the rounds drew it in place of a Salesforce step's card); the step's two connection handles are kept beside the slot inside a transparent box with the card's 1 px border, so they sit where the real card places them. The canvas, its header, the handles and the cards around it are the product as it is today, not decisions.
Google Drive's mark is drawn inline as an SVG; the build draws the same SVG.
